title: Rust Programming
description: Beginner-to-advanced Rust reference covering ownership, borrowing, enums, traits, generics, collections, iterators, errors, concurrency, async, unsafe boundaries, testing, Cargo, and production engineering.

subtopics.title: Ownership, Moves & Copy
subtopics.description: Every value has one owner; moving transfers responsibility unless the type is Copy. Values are dropped deterministically when their owner leaves scope.

callouts.title: Borrow Unless Ownership Is Required
callouts.text: Accept &str, &[T], or &Path for read-only inputs. Return owned values when the caller must retain independent data.

subtopics.title: Borrowing & Lifetimes
subtopics.description: References cannot outlive their referents. Lifetime parameters describe relationships; they do not extend runtime lifetime.

callouts.title: Fix Ownership Design Before Adding Clones
callouts.text: Clone is valid when independent ownership is intentional. Repeated cloning to appease the compiler often hides unclear ownership or an overlong borrow.

subtopics.title: Structs, Enums & Pattern Matching
subtopics.description: Enums carry data per variant and pair with exhaustive match to model state machines and result domains without null sentinels.

subtopics.title: Traits, Generics & Trait Objects
subtopics.description: Generic bounds use static dispatch and specialization per concrete type; dyn Trait enables runtime polymorphism behind a pointer.

codeBlocks.code:
fn render<T: Display>(value: &T) -> String { value.to_string() }

struct Pipeline { stages: Vec<Box<dyn Stage + Send + Sync>> }

callouts.title: Prefer Capabilities over Concrete Types
callouts.text: Small focused traits make code testable. Use impl Trait/generics by default and dyn Trait when heterogeneous runtime composition is required.

subtopics.title: Collections & Iterator Pipelines
subtopics.description: Vec is contiguous, HashMap indexes keys, HashSet enforces uniqueness, and iterators lazily compose transformations until consumed.

subtopics.title: Option, Result & Error Context
subtopics.description: Option represents absence; Result represents recoverable failure. The ? operator returns early while converting compatible errors.

callouts.title: panic Is Not Routine Error Handling
callouts.text: Return Result for expected operational failures. Reserve panic for violated invariants or unrecoverable programmer defects.

subtopics.title: Threads, Send, Sync & Shared State
subtopics.description: Send permits ownership transfer across threads; Sync permits shared references across threads. Arc shares ownership; Mutex or RwLock guards mutation.

callouts.title: Do Not Hold Locks Across Slow Work
callouts.text: Keep critical sections small and never hold a synchronous lock across .await. Prefer message passing when one task can own mutable state.

subtopics.title: async, Futures & Cancellation
subtopics.description: An async function returns a lazy Future that progresses when polled by an executor. Dropping a future cancels further polling, so cleanup and cancellation safety matter.

callouts.title: Bound Every Queue and External Call
callouts.text: Use timeouts, concurrency limits, backpressure, and cancellation tokens. Detached tasks otherwise become hidden resource owners.

subtopics.title: unsafe & FFI Boundaries
subtopics.description: unsafe enables raw pointers, unsafe calls, mutable statics, unsafe traits, and union fields. It transfers proof obligations to the programmer rather than disabling Rust's type system.

codeBlocks.code:
// SAFETY: ptr is non-null, aligned, initialized, and valid for len elements.
let slice = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(ptr, len) };

callouts.title: Make Unsafe Tiny and Auditable
callouts.text: Wrap unsafe internals in a safe API whose invariants are documented and tested with sanitizers or Miri where applicable.

subtopics.title: Cargo, Workspaces & Features
subtopics.description: Cargo.lock pins applications; libraries publish compatible version ranges. Features are additive compile-time capabilities and should not represent mutually exclusive modes.

subtopics.title: Unit, Integration & Documentation Tests
subtopics.description: Keep unit tests beside private code, integration tests under tests/, examples in documentation, and benchmark performance-sensitive behavior.

subtopics.title: Production Checklist
subtopics.description: Format, lint, audit dependencies, minimize unsafe, instrument latency and errors, test shutdown, and define ownership for every task and resource.

codeBlocks.code:
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo test --all-features
cargo audit

callouts.title: Release Review
callouts.text: Pin the toolchain, commit Cargo.lock for deployable apps, deny warnings in CI, redact secrets, bound memory/concurrency, preserve error context, and test cross-platform targets.
